result.source_concept: Child learning to sort fruit at a market

mappings.source_element: Tagged fruit pieces given to the child
mappings.relation: Analogous to supervised learning where examples have known outputs
mappings.evidence: “First, you give them tagged pieces and they practice filling baskets.”

mappings.source_element: Child practicing filling baskets with tagged fruit
mappings.target_element: Algorithm learning a mapping from input features to outputs
mappings.relation: Both involve learning a function that maps inputs to correct labels

mappings.source_element: Tagless crate of fruit that arrives later
mappings.target_element: Unlabeled data used for unsupervised learning
mappings.relation: Analogous to discovering inherent structure without explicit labels
mappings.evidence: “Then a tagless crate arrives, and they group by what seems alike.”

mappings.source_element: Child grouping fruit by perceived similarity
mappings.target_element: Algorithm clustering or extracting patterns from unlabeled data
mappings.relation: Both perform pattern discovery based on similarity

mappings.source_element: Child quickly placing a new piece of fruit into the correct basket
mappings.target_element: Model making predictions or classifications on new, unseen data
mappings.relation: Both apply learned knowledge to novel instances
mappings.evidence: “when a new piece appears, they place it quickly and confidently.”

result.process_summary: Both the child and a machine‑learning system first learn from explicit, labeled examples (supervised learning), then infer structure from unlabeled examples (unsupervised learning), and finally use the acquired knowledge to categorize or predict outcomes for new, unseen items.
potential_breaks: A child may rely on prior world knowledge or visual cues that do not map to high‑dimensional feature spaces used by algorithms.
The analogy suggests a strict sequential order (supervised then unsupervised), whereas many ML pipelines combine or skip stages.
Human intuition can handle ambiguous cases more flexibly than current models, so the confidence described may overstate model performance.
